verdict.rationale: Both diffs make the same correct change: they build a Map from normalized email to index once and register appended contacts so duplicates inside the upload still merge. This preserves first-entry-wins, original position and arrival order. A also adds a regression test that pins first-entry-wins when the existing book already has duplicate emails, the rule the index could most easily break, plus a short comment explaining why the first index is kept. B checked equivalence with a 2,000-case random comparison, but nothing in the repo protects that behavior from future regressions.
a_issues: The benchmark harness is not committed, so the timing claim cannot be reproduced from the repo (this is acceptable).
b_issues: No test covers first-entry-wins when the existing book has duplicate emails; the random equivalence check was thrown away rather than kept as a test.
No comment explains why the Map keeps only the first index per email, which is a subtle way of matching the old findIndex behavior.

verdict.rationale: The two `src/import.ts` changes are functionally identical: a normalized-email Map built once, first existing entry wins, and new contacts are added to the map as they are appended, so behavior is preserved and the O(n·m) scan is gone. B also adds a regression test that pins the first-entry-wins rule for duplicate emails already in the book, which is the behavior the index could most easily break. B's short comment explains why the `has` check exists. A checked the same rule only with a throwaway randomized comparison that it did not keep, so nothing in the repo protects it.
a_issues: No test protects the first-existing-entry-wins rule for duplicate emails already in the book; the equivalence check was a deleted throwaway script.
b_issues: The one-line `if` without braces differs slightly in style from the rest of the function (minor).
